success_patterns: Three of the eight clues (the tambourine, Colleen McCullough and Adirondacks clues) were solved by finding the clue repeated verbatim in an archive or flashcard passage (jedoublen/jeopardy GitHub dump, J! Archive, StudyStack). The agent copied the answer shown after the clue. When J! Archive showed only the clue, a flashcard passage supplied the answer.

For clues with no archive hit (the Michael Nobel, Liberty Bell and 1931 gland clues), the agent anchored on the clue's most distinctive detail. It picked the one entity the passages tie to that detail (Alfred Nobel 'born in Stockholm'; 'Pennsylvania is misspelled on the Liberty Bell'; 'chemists discovered that the pituitary gland contains a hormone'). It ignored topic-level noise.

Answers matched the slot type the clue names: 'this 1997 movie' gave the film and not the actor, 'this capital city' gave the city, 'this gland' gave 'pituitary gland' with its head noun, and a bare modifier-free name was used for the range ('Adirondacks').
A clue asking for a specific part of a name ('Last name of the French brothers...') was answered with only that part ('Michelin'), not 'Michelin brothers' or 'Andre Michelin'.
Media cues in the clue ('heard here') were ignored as decoration. The agent matched the textual remainder of the clue to the archived line.

patch.reasoning: Most successes are already explained by Rules 2-4. Two small gaps appear in the successes. First, clues that ask for a specific part of a name ('Last name of ...') need a short explicit rule. Second, 'heard here' / 'seen here' phrases come from audio or video clues, and archived copies keep them verbatim. An earlier version of the second note was bundled with many other edits and rejected, so I keep both edits short and non-overlapping.

edits.target: Still apply the person-name rule above.
edits.content: - Part-of-name clues ('Last name of the French brothers who...', 'First name of...', 'Initials of...', 'Surname of...'): give ONLY the requested part ('Michelin'), never the full name, the family or group label ('Michelin brothers'), or a single member's full name ('Andre Michelin').

edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Media cues in the clue ('heard here', 'seen here', 'shown here', 'pictured') refer to an audio or video clue you cannot perceive. They are decoration. Archive copies of the clue keep these words, so match the remaining textual hooks ('wandering minstrel', 'handheld percussion instrument') against the passages and copy the archived answer ('tambourine').
